policy: Every flag is a fact observed on an official 2026-11-18 read or a drift against a committed artifact. Flags are published on the Flagged for Review page with their source link; they never block the build and are never patched into canonical data.

flags.item: Arden Key (IND, DE) game-status designation changed between the 2026-11-13 canonical capture and the 2026-11-18 fresh read
flags.finding: The committed canonical row (nfl-availability-28ef/data/injuries-week10-2026.csv) carries Arden Key = Hamstring / Full Participation in Practice / Questionable. The 2026-11-18 fresh read of https://www.nfl.com/injuries/league/2026/REG10 shows Arden Key with blank Injuries and blank Game Status (Full Participation in Practice only). This is a material designation change on a single row.
flags.action: Flagged, not patched. The canonical file is a 2026-11-13 snapshot and is left as-is; the fresh value is published on the injuries page.
flags.blocks: DR-21 (injury-hub read with clock time / delta)

flags.item: Week 11 injury report is not yet published as of the 2026-11-18 capture
flags.finding: https://www.nfl.com/injuries/league/2026/REG11 redirects server-side to REG10 (Week 10). https://www.nfl.com/injuries/2026/reg11/ returns 404 'Flag on the Play'. The /injuries/ hub's WEEK 1–11 selector lists Week 11, but the page still renders Week 10. Captured 2026-11-18T03:46:15Z (Wednesday night ET, ahead of the Week 11 Thursday game).
flags.action: Recorded as a timing fact. The Week 11 report should be re-read after the NFL publishes it (typically Wednesday of the game week).

flags.item: Prior VR-17/VR-26 flag (Ravens stale QB depth) does not reproduce on the 2026-11-18 live injury page
flags.finding: The brief's flag said Baltimore still published Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley at QB after both went on injured reserve. The 2026-11-18 Ravens table on https://www.nfl.com/injuries/league/2026/REG10 lists 10 players and neither Lamar Jackson nor Tyler Huntley appears. This is recorded as a change against the earlier flag, not as a resolution of the underlying transactions question (which needs the official transactions log, not the injury page).
flags.action: Flagged as a change vs the earlier flag. The transactions-log verification that VR-17/VR-26 actually asked for is still outstanding and is not closed by this observation.

flags.item: Standings snapshot drift vs the 2026-11-17 canonical file is fully explained by the Week 10 Monday game
flags.finding: The fresh 2026-11-18 standings read differs from data/nfl-standings-2026-11-17.csv in 8 cells, all on Baltimore Ravens and Los Angeles Chargers. The 11-17 file is annotated 'pre Week 10 MNF'; the 8-cell drift is exactly the LAC@BAL Monday Night Football result (Nov 16): BAL 4-5→4-6, LAC 0-8→1-8, with matching PF/PA/STRK changes. No contradiction; the older snapshot is simply one game behind.
flags.action: Recorded as explained drift. The stale file is left untouched; the fresh read is the current value.

flags.item: Week 11 has 6 byes, so any 32-club reconciliation must expect 26 active clubs
flags.finding: The 2026-11-18 Week 11 schedule read lists 13 games and 6 bye clubs (ATL, CLE, GB, LAR, NE, SEA), i.e. 26 clubs playing. Any per-club availability or depth reconciliation for Week 11 must expect 26 active clubs, not 32.
flags.action: Recorded as a scope fact for the 32-team sweep requirement.

flags.item: Two canonical standings snapshots coexist with different recency; the older one is still referenced by the site pipeline
flags.finding: data/nfl-standings-2026.csv holds a pre-Week-10-MNF snapshot (BUF 7-1) while data/nfl-standings-2026-11-17.csv holds the post-Week-10-Sunday snapshot (BUF 8-1). scripts/nfl_extract.py writes data/nfl-standings-week10-2026.csv and research/nfl/review.py reads it, so more than one standings artifact is in play. The fresh 2026-11-18 read matches the 11-17 file on all non-MNF rows. This is an irregularity in artifact recency, not a data contradiction.
flags.action: Flagged for review. Not patched; the desk publishes the fresh 2026-11-18 read as the current value and leaves the canonical files as historical snapshots.
